prompt:
Use the attached clay render as the exact blueprint. Keep every wall, opening, window, cornice, skirting, floor and ceiling line, the camera height, lens and angle, and the position, size and angle of every furniture piece and built-in exactly as in the clay. Move, resize, add or remove nothing. Each placeholder shape in the clay marks one product listed below; render it there at the stated size. Only turn the clay into real materials and light. The other attached images are close-ups of the exact products: match their form, colour and texture. Positions are fractions of frame width (x) and height (y) from the top-left.

1. PHOTO. Top Scandinavian interiors magazine: the entrance hall of a Nordic garden house, 3 pm mid-winter, 24 mm shift lens at 1.2 m, level, straight verticals, all sharp. A threshold of light: the bright living room through the door, left third; the console vignette, right third.

2. LIGHT. No window here. A frosted roof light just above the frame, over the bench, pours soft top light down the left wall. The hall walls soft white, two thirds of a stop under the living room's back wall. The living room through the door is the brightest area, still detailed; its daylight spills a pale fan across the threshold floor and up the oak portal. The facing wall darkens gently toward the right corner. The console pieces catch the top light from the upper left, each with a soft shadow on the wall to its right; dense contact shadows. Ceiling a touch darker, darkest top right. No sun patch. Real contrast, never milky. 4600 K: whites white, never cream, pink or grey. One lamp, 2700 K, shadowless: the fabric cube glows evenly and fans soft warm light on the wall around it.

3. MATERIALS. Matte mineral paint #F4F1EC, faint chalky movement. Wide oiled white-oak planks, pale honey #D6BF9E, running through the threshold. Bench, console, portal: oiled light oak #C8A27A, satin sheen, a long soft highlight along the console top and down the planks to the door.

4. PRODUCTS, one per line, each on its clay placeholder:
a. ART, x 0.62-0.74, y 0.16-0.42: a 45 x 55 print, one loose black ink line on cream, wide cream mat, slim black frame, no glare.
b. VASE, console right end, x 0.73-0.78: 26 cm matte textured warm-white ceramic, 3-5 slender dried stems in sage and oat.
c. TRAY, console middle, x 0.67-0.73: empty slim oval tray, matte black metal, flat.
d. PEGS on the left wall at 1.7 m: four light pine oval pegs in a row, empty, no rail.
e. WALL LAMP above them: a 15 cm warm-white fabric cube, hardwired, no cable.
f. BENCH CUSHION, cut by the left edge: warm off-white linen-look flat cushion, 3 cm thin.
g. THROW at the bench's corner end: white cotton waffle blanket folded into a neat square, as wide as the bench is deep.
h. BASKET under the bench's corner end: empty 30 cm coiled rope basket, top third warm-white cotton, jute below, rim below the seat.
i. THROUGH THE DOOR, exactly the living room of reference 1: three prints between two glowing travertine cubes over the oatmeal sofa, the ribbed silk lantern, the seagrass basket, the white flat-woven rug; no floor lamp, nothing on the wall left of the sofa.

5. NOT IN FRAME: table lamp, umbrella stand, mirror, boxes, plant, coats, bags, shoes, keys, books, glass, socket, cable, text, people. No bloom, haze, rays, halos, HDR, grain or vignette.
